headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading errors: cognee’s sensitive support data can flow into Kestra’s broad networked workflows and actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests customer support data, documents, and workflows, while Kestra reads files and runs declarative workflows with stdin/stdout and broad task surfaces. If cognee outputs are copied into Kestra inputs or shared storage, prompt-like content could steer downstream tasks. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are placed into a Kestra workflow file or stdin input, THEN instruction-like content can influence task execution.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or message handoff, THEN prompt injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Restrict Kestra inputs to structured schemas only.
Strip instructions from cognee-generated text before handoff.
Use a quarantine folder for any transferred artifacts.
Add a human review step before Kestra executes imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents; Kestra has broad network egress and can read/write files plus send data to Slack, email, cloud, and other services. If the pair shares a workspace or handoff path, sensitive data from cognee can be exfiltrated by Kestra to third parties. The profiles do not show isolation between them, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are written into a Kestra-accessible workspace, THEN sensitive support or finance data can be transmitted onward.
IF Kestra tasks forward those artifacts to email, Slack, cloud storage, or HTTP endpoints, THEN leakage occurs.
mitigations: Disable Kestra tasks that forward transferred artifacts externally.
Use separate storage locations for cognee and Kestra.
Redact personal and finance data before any handoff.
Limit Kestra network destinations to an allowlist.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of sensitive fields.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and Kestra can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem with elevated root/docker.sock requests. If both operate on the same directory or mutable workflow artifacts, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite outputs. The profiles show overlapping write-adjacent behavior and no locking mechanism, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or workflow artifact set, THEN race conditions and overwrite conflicts can occur.
IF Kestra runs shell tasks against cognee-managed files, THEN concurrent mutation can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue.
Make shared artifacts read-only for one side.
Run Kestra without root or docker.sock where possible.
Snapshot files before any cross-agent write step.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra is an automation/orchestration system that can send emails, Slack messages, and trigger cloud or shell actions, while cognee produces decisions, workflows, and expert SQL queries. If Kestra treats cognee output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated output can cascade into real actions. Because downstream action-taking is explicit in Kestra and verification is not documented, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes cognee-generated decisions or workflows without validation, THEN incorrect outputs can trigger downstream actions.
IF those actions include email, Slack, cloud, or shell execution, THEN the error propagates beyond a single document.
mitigations: Require schema validation on cognee outputs.
Add a manual approval gate before action tasks.
Log and diff all imported decisions before execution.
Use dry-run mode for new cross-agent workflows.
Reject free-form text as an execution source.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Kestra can route data to email, Slack, cloud storage, and logs. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the pair is used on regulated data. The profiles do not document HIPAA/GDPR/DPA alignment, so the compliance risk is real but not proven severe enough for high.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or finance data is routed from cognee into Kestra logs, notifications, or cloud services, THEN retention/residency obligations may be violated.
IF deletion or export requests must be honored across both systems, THEN mismatched retention can block compliance.
mitigations: Classify data before any transfer.
Disable logging of sensitive payloads in Kestra.
Route regulated data only to approved regions/services.
Document retention and deletion handling for both systems.
Add a compliance review for any new data flow.
